candidates.title: Point-based liver and hepatic tumor segmentation and estimation
candidates.abstract:
Liver cancer is the fifth most common cancer in the world. Liver cancer is more serious in areas of western and central Africa and eastern and southeastern Asia. The average incidence of liver cancer in these areas is 20 per 100,000, and liver cancer is the third highest death cause from cancer. Roughly 20,000 new cases of liver cancer are diagnosed every year in the USA. If a very small lump tumor is found by early detection, treatment and curing may be easy, and human life can be prolonged. 
In this dissertation, point-based liver and hepatic tumor segmentation and estimation are presented in contrast enhanced (CE)-computed tomography (CT) images. Without having a reference image and training data, fully automatic segmentation of the liver structure and tumors using a reference point based on the spine is processed. Segmentation of the liver structure and tumors is performed regardless of pixel variation of CE-CT images involved by contrast agent. 
After obtaining CE-CT images, pre-processing such as histogram transformation and adaptive multi-modal threshold is performed. In order to process fully automatic segmentation for the liver structure and tumors, a reference point from the spine is defined. Liver segmentation using C-class maximum a posteriori decision and binary morphological filtering is processed. Partial histogram threshold algorithms are proposed in order to perform better liver segmentation. 
Finally, an inner small tumor is found, and large inner tumors using two statistical optimal thresholds are segmented. Boundary tumors of the liver are extracted by the bounding box and convex hull. Segmented tumors are evaluated by four basic possibilities, such as true negative, false positive, false negative, and true positive. As the evaluation measure, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy are calculated.

candidates.title: Liver And Hepatic Tumors Segmentation In 3-D Ct Images
candidates.abstract: Medical imaging is an important technique for diagnosis and treatment planning today. A new proposed method of fully automatic processing frameworks is given based on graph-cut and Geodesic Graph cut algorithms. This paper addresses the problem of segmenting liver and tumor regions from the abdominal CT images. A predicate is defined for measuring the evidence for a boundary between two regions using Geodesic Graph-based representation of the image. The algorithm is applied to image segmentation using two different kinds of local neighborhoods in constructing the graph. Liver and hepatic tumor segmentation can be automatically processed by the Geodesic graph-cut based method. This system has concentrated on finding a fast and interactive segmentation method for liver and tumor segmentation. In the preprocessing stage, the CT image process is carried over with mean shift filter and statistical thresholding method for reducing processing area with improving detections rate. Second stage is liver segmentation; the liver region has been segmented using the algorithm of the proposed method. The next stage tumor segmentation also followed the same steps. Finally the liver and tumor regions are separately segmented from the computer tomography image.

candidates.title: Hepatic Vein and Arterial Vessel Segmentation in Liver Tumor Patients
candidates.abstract: Preoperative observation of liver status in patients with liver tumors by abdominal Computed Tomography (CT) imaging is one of the essential references for formulating surgical plans. Preoperative vessel segmentation in the patient's liver region has become an increasingly important and challenging problem. Almost all existing methods first segment arterial and venous vessels on CT in the arterial and venous phases, respectively. Then, the two are directly registered to complete the reconstruction of the vascular system, ignoring the displacement and deformation of blood vessels caused by changes in body position and respiration in the two phases. We propose an unsupervised domain-adaptive two-stage vessel segmentation framework for simultaneous fine segmentation of arterial and venous vessels on venous phase CT. Specifically, we first achieve domain adaptation for arterial and venous phase CT using a modified cycle-consistent adversarial network. The newly added discriminator can improve the ability to generate and discriminate tiny blood vessels, making the domain-adaptive network more robust. The second-stage supervised training of arterial vessels was then performed on the translated arterial phase CT. In this process, we propose an orthogonal depth projection loss function to enhance the representation ability of the 3D U-shape segmentation network for the geometric information of the vessel model. The segmented venous vessels were also performed on venous phase CT in the second stage. Finally, we invited professional doctors to annotate arterial and venous vessels on the venous phase CT of the test set. The experimental results show that the segmentation accuracy of arterial and venous vessels on venous phase CT is 0.8454 and 0.8087, respectively. Our proposed framework can simultaneously achieve supervised segmentation of venous vessels and unsupervised segmentation of arterial vessels on venous phase CT. Our approach can be extended to other fields of medical segmentation, such as unsupervised domain adaptive segmentation of liver tumors at different CT phases, to facilitate the development of the community.

candidates.title: Deep segmentation of the liver and the hepatic tumors from abdomen tomography images
candidates.abstract: A pipelined framework is proposed for accurate, automated, simultaneous segmentation of the liver as well as the hepatic tumors from computed tomography (CT) images. The introduced framework composed of three pipelined levels. First, two different transfers deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) are applied to get high-level compact features of CT images. Second, a pixel-wise classifier is used to obtain two output-classified maps for each CNN model. Finally, a fusion neural network (FNN) is used to integrate the two maps. Experimentations performed on the MICCAI’2017 database of the liver tumor segmentation (LITS) challenge, result in a dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 93.5% for the segmentation of the liver and of 74.40% for the segmentation of the lesion, using a 5-fold cross-validation scheme. Comparative results with the state-of-the-art techniques on the same data show the competing performance of the proposed framework for simultaneous liver and tumor segmentation.

candidates.title: Segmentations of Liver and Hepatic Tumors from 3D Computed Tomography Abdominal Images
candidates.abstract: The segmentation of liver using computed tomography (CT) data has gained a lot of importance in the medical image processing field. In this paper, we present a survey on liver segmentation methods and techniques using CT images for liver segmentation. An adaptive initialization method was developed to produce fully automatic processing frameworks based on graph-cut and gradient flow active contour algorithms. This method was applied to abdominal Computed Tomography (CT) images for segmentation of liver tissue and hepatic tumors. Twenty-five anonymized datasets were randomly collected from several radiology centres without specific request on acquisition parameter settings nor patient clinical situation as inclusion criteria. Resulting automatic segmentations of liver tissue and tumors were compared to their reference standard delineations manually performed by a specialist. Segmentation accuracy has been assessed through the following evaluation framework: dice similarity coefficient, false negative ratio, false positive ratio and processing time. The implemented initialization method allows fully automatic segmentation leading to superior overall performances of graph-cut algorithm in terms of accuracy and processing time. The initialization method here presented resulted suitable and reliable for two different segmentation techniques and could be further extended.

candidates.title: Fast segmentation and modeling of hepatic components for the planning of robot-assisted liver tumor ablation
candidates.abstract: Segmentation and modeling of hepatic components from pre-operative images is very important for treatment planning and guidance in robot-assisted liver tumor ablation. An in-house developed system for hepatic component segmentation and modeling using CT data is presented in this paper. This system includes gross liver segmentation by a 3D mesh deformation model, liver vasculature segmentation by a vessel context-based voting and grouping method, liver tumor segmentation by a support vector machine framework, and other segmentation/modeling tool. This system was tested using 20 data sets from human patients and 5 sets of porcine CT scan. It is suggested by experimental results that the developed system is able to conduct fast segmentation and modeling of hepatic components for both human and large animal, with a satisfying accuracy, to support treatment planning.

candidates.title: A model integrating CEA and KRAS mutation statuses and computed tomography tumor-habitat radiomics predicts synchronous liver metastases in patients with rectal cancer: a dual-center study
candidates.abstract: Objective To investigate the diagnostic performance of a computed tomography (CT)-based habitat radiomics model for discriminating between patients with rectal cancer (RC) with and without synchronous liver metastases (SLM). Methods This retrospective study enrolled two independent patient cohorts. Cohort 1 (internal cohort) included 198 patients with pathologically confirmed RC with complete CT data from April 2022 to June 2025, comprising 46 SLM-positive and 152 SLM-negative cases. This cohort was divided randomly in a 7:3 ratio into a training set (140 patients: 33 SLM-positive, 107 SLM-negative) and an internal validation set (58 patients: 13 SLM-positive, 45 SLM-negative). Cohort 2 served as an external validation set, consisting of 55 patients with RC (18 SLM-positive, 37 SLM-negative). Regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated manually slice-by-slice on arterial-phase thin-slice CT images. Raw radiomics features were extracted from the ROIs and K-means clustering was implemented to segment tumor sub-habitats, followed by feature extraction for each sub-habitat. Feature-dimensionality reduction was performed on the training set using minimum redundancy maximum relevance and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator algorithms. Logistic regression classifiers were constructed to develop a conventional radiomics model and a habitat radiomics model, respectively. Model performance and clinical utility were quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified serum CEA and KRAS mutations as independent risk factors for SLM. These were integrated to build a clinical baseline model with AUC values of 0.730 (training set), 0.724 (internal validation set), and 0.701 (external validation set). After rigorous feature screening, 13 conventional radiomics features and 13 habitat radiomics features were retained for model construction. The conventional radiomics model yielded AUCs of 0.785 (training), 0.764 (internal validation), and 0.782 (external validation), while the habitat radiomics model achieved higher AUCs, with AUCs of 0.862, 0.826, and 0.826, respectively. The combined model integrating independent clinical risk factors and habitat radiomics score attained the numerically highest AUCs, with AUCs of 0.883 (training), 0.846 (internal validation), and 0.851 (external validation), outperforming the clinical, conventional radiomics, and standalone habitat models with robust cross-cohort stability. Calibration curves demonstrated favorable predictive consistency of the combined model, while DCA revealed sustained clinical net benefit across broad risk-threshold ranges. Conclusion A CT-based habitat radiomics model could effectively identify patients with RC with SLM, with performance numerically better than that of conventional whole-tumor radiomics. Integrating clinical biomarkers with habitat radiomics further increased the predictive accuracy, offering a novel non-invasive preoperative risk-stratification strategy for RC.

candidates.title: Nutritional value and total quality of sour curry powder, the most popular southern Thailand dish
candidates.abstract: As cross-cultural interactions continuously transform global dietary habits, the traditional Japanese rice seasoning (furikake) offers an innovative blueprint for Thai food product development. Inspired by this concept, a novel instant Thai sour curry rice topping was formulated. This product successfully integrates a high-protein nutritional profile with superior consumer palatability and extended storage stability. Key ingredients for Southern Thai sour curry paste including hot chili (Capsicum frutescens L.) shallot (Allium ascalonicum L.), garlic bulb (Allium sativum L.), lemongrass (Cymbopogon citratus (DC.) Stapf), and salt were blended, mixed with pre-cooked fish meat and souring agents tamarind pulp (Tamarindus indica L.) and dried cowa leaves (dried Garcinia cowa Roxb. ex Choisy leaves), stir-fried, and subsequently dried to yield the instant product. Results revealed that the combination of tamarind pulp and dried G. cowa Roxb leaves as a souring agent achieved the highest sensory acceptability (92%) and demonstrated high antioxidant activity. Nutritional analysis reveals that the final dehydrated product is rich in protein, yielding 39.45 ± 0.24%, while unsaturated fatty acids constitute a substantial portion (5.59 ± 0.05%) of the total lipid content (9.62 ± 0.08%). Furthermore, the sequential thermal treatment of stir-frying followed by hot air oven drying effectively minimized the microbial count, successfully complying with the safety standards established by the Thai FDA.

candidates.title: AI-assisted image-based screening identifies TFEB agonists that restore adipose angiogenesis and reduce adipose fibrosis
candidates.abstract: Adipose tissue expansion in obesity frequently outpaces vascularization, triggering hypoxia, fibrosis, and metabolic dysfunction. The molecular mechanisms coordinating adaptive angiogenesis during this expansion remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that myeloid deletion of Transcription Factor EB ( Tfeb ) in high-fat diet-fed mice exacerbates epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) dysfunction, manifesting as profound hypoxia, fibrosis, and systemic insulin resistance. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays reveal a novel TFEB-VEGFA axis: TFEB directly activates Vegfa transcription in macrophages, and its absence impairs angiogenic compensation under hypoxic stress. To translate these findings, we established an AI-driven, high-content screening platform to quantify TFEB nuclear translocation. We identified and validated Tetrandrine and Pacritinib as potent TFEB agonists. Notably, Tetrandrine acts via an mTOR-independent mechanism. Pharmacological activation of TFEB with these compounds restored adipose angiogenesis, resolved fibrosis, and improved insulin sensitivity in obese mice. These findings establish macrophage TFEB as a critical regulator of healthy adipose remodeling and validate the TFEB-VEGFA axis as a therapeutic target for metabolic diseases.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence in pancreatic cancer surgery: evidence maturity, boundaries, and clinical translation
candidates.abstract: Pancreatic cancer surgery requires decisions about resectability, treatment sequencing, operative planning, complications, and prognosis. We mapped artificial intelligence (AI) studies to five surgical decision domains and evaluated study design, validation, performance, decision utility, workflow fit, and evidence limitations. This structured narrative review included 31 direct AI studies and three adjacent or protocol studies; only direct AI studies underwent evidence-maturity grading. Eighteen studies met Level 1, ten Level 2, and three Level 3; none reached Levels 4 or 5. Three-dimensional assessment of vascular involvement has undergone external and prospective performance validation, but its effect on surgical decisions or patient outcomes remains unproven. Automated segmentation can aid anatomical visualization, although tumor delineation and workflow demands limit use. Transcriptomic analyses of trial samples suggest differential adjuvant treatment benefit but do not establish prospective biomarker-guided treatment allocation. Models for complications, recurrence, and survival offer risk-stratification signals, yet calibration, actionable thresholds, class imbalance, and clinical utility remain concerns. AI should support radiologists, surgeons, and multidisciplinary teams rather than replace their judgment. Clinical adoption requires robust external validation, prospective workflow assessment, and evidence that AI-assisted decisions improve patient outcomes.

candidates.title: CXCR2 associated neutrophil stromal interactions and immune exclusion in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer
candidates.abstract: Most microsatellite-stable or mismatch-repair-proficient colorectal cancers respond poorly to immune checkpoint monotherapy. This Mini Review examines whether C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (CXCR2)-associated neutrophil recruitment and local stromal interactions contribute to immune exclusion: CD8+ T cells accumulate in stroma or at the tumor margin with limited entry into epithelial nests. We propose that, in a subset of excluded lesions, recruited neutrophils acquire local functions that impair T-cell activity or access. Human observations and experimental perturbations support parts of this model; the complete pathway has not been established as a major cause of checkpoint resistance. Recruitment dependence, tissue adaptation, and measured function provide a basis for comparing studies with different neutrophil labels. Lesions selected for mechanistic investigation would need confirmed microsatellite-stable or mismatch-repair-proficient status, spatial exclusion, and a relevant intratumoral CXCR2-associated neutrophil program. Primary tumors and metastatic sites require separate evaluation. The limited activity of navarixin plus pembrolizumab argues against unselected targeting. Combining CXCR2 inhibition, selected stromal or vascular modulation, and checkpoint blockade remains a preclinical hypothesis. Before clinical translation, comparative studies must link intratumoral target engagement to improved CD8+ T-cell access, function, and tumor control. The proposed tissue biomarkers are research tools whose predictive value requires validation.
